name: STROBE (Combined Checklist)
source: von Elm E, Altman DG, Egger M, Pocock SJ, Gotzsche PC, Vandenbroucke JP; STROBE Initiative. The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) Statement: Guidelines for Reporting Observational Studies. PLoS Med. 2007;4(10):e296. https://www.strobe-statement.org/checklists/ | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2020495/

items.text: State the observational study design using a standard term in the title or abstract.
Provide a balanced, informative abstract summarizing study methods and key findings.
Explain the scientific background and rationale for the observational study.
State specific study objectives, including any pre-specified hypotheses.
Summarize key elements of the observational study design early in the report.
Describe study settings, locations, and dates of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection.
Specify eligibility criteria, participant selection or case-control ascertainment methods, and follow-up procedures.
For matched cohort or case-control studies, state matching criteria and exposed-unexposed or control-per-case ratios.
Define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, confounders, effect modifiers, and diagnostic criteria.
Describe data sources and measurement methods for each variable, noting comparability across groups.
Describe efforts taken to identify and address potential sources of bias.
Explain how the study sample size was determined.
Explain how quantitative variables were analyzed and justify any groupings chosen.
Describe all statistical methods, including approaches used to control for confounding.
Describe methods used to evaluate subgroups and statistical interactions.
Explain how missing data were handled in the analysis.
Explain design-specific adjustments for loss to follow-up, case-control matching, or sampling strategy.
Describe any sensitivity analyses performed.
Report participant counts at each stage from potentially eligible through follow-up and final analysis.
State reasons for non-participation at each stage of the study.
Consider presenting participant flow in a diagram.
Summarize participant demographics, clinical features, exposures, and potential confounders.
Report the number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest.
For cohort studies, summarize average and total follow-up duration.
Report outcome event counts or summary measures (or exposure counts for case-control studies).
Report unadjusted and confounder-adjusted estimates with precision, specifying which confounders were included and why.
State category boundaries whenever continuous variables were categorized.
Consider translating relative risk estimates into absolute risk over a meaningful time period.
Report results of subgroup, interaction, and sensitivity analyses.
Summarize the main findings in relation to the study objectives.
Discuss study limitations, addressing direction and magnitude of potential bias or imprecision.
Give a cautious overall interpretation considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity, and prior evidence.
Discuss external validity and generalizability of the study findings.
State funding sources and funders' roles for the current and any parent study.
